evals.name: app-uses-bitnami-redis-helm
evals.prompt: our app uses a bitnami redis helm release in sentinel mode (redis 8.0.2, 3 nodes) for its background job queues. I want to get off bitnami and onto valkey 9. my plan: deploy a valkey statefulset, run REPLICAOF pointing at the current redis master, wait for sync, then repoint the app and kill the old release. cluster is air-gapped (internal registry mirror, no internet from nodes). does this plan work? if not what should I do instead? write your answer to answer.md
evals.expected_output: Must reject REPLICAOF (Redis 8.x writes RDB v12 which Valkey cannot parse; also the replica flushes itself before rejecting). Must recommend logical replay (RedisShake sync/rdb reader or rdb-cli), stress queue data must be transferred not flushed, cover air-gap delivery (static binary tarball or ghcr image to mirror), and note the Valkey 9 one-way door / keep final RDB as rollback.
assertions: States that the proposed REPLICAOF-based sync will not work, and attributes the failure to the RDB/snapshot format incompatibility between Redis 8.x and Valkey rather than to networking, auth, or air-gap issues
Warns that pointing a Valkey instance at the Redis source destroys/empties the Valkey dataset before the format rejection is detected, so it must not be attempted as a trial

Recommends a logical/command-replay transfer path (e.g. RedisShake or rdb-cli) that decodes the data and re-issues normal commands, instead of REPLICAOF, DUMP/RESTORE, MIGRATE, or copying dump.rdb into Valkey
Treats the background job queue data as must-transfer (or explicitly drained to empty under maintenance mode) rather than acceptable to lose in a fresh start

Explains how the chosen migration tool and Valkey images reach the air-gapped cluster (mirroring the image(s) into the internal registry and/or side-loading the tool binary), rather than assuming nodes can download them
States that Valkey 9 snapshots cannot be loaded by Redis or older Valkey, and instructs keeping/archiving the final pre-cutover Redis RDB as the rollback artifact before deleting the old release

evals.name: translate-these-bitnami-redis-chart
evals.prompt:
translate these bitnami redis chart values to the groundhog2k valkey chart for me and flag anything that behaves differently:

architecture: replication
auth:
  enabled: true
  sentinel: true
  existingSecret: my-redis-secret
sentinel:
  enabled: true
  masterSet: mymaster
  quorum: 2
  downAfterMilliseconds: 60000
replica:
  replicaCount: 3
master:
  persistence:
    enabled: true
    size: 8Gi
metrics:
  enabled: true

write the translated values.yaml plus a list of behavioral differences to answer.md
evals.expected_output: Translated values using haMode block (enabled, replicas 3, quorum 2, downAfterMilliseconds 60000 with failoverWait raised >60s, masterGroupName: mymaster), auth expressed as config-file fragments via extraSecretValkeyConfigs/sentinelConfig (NOT a bare password secret), storage.requestedSize: 8Gi, metrics.enabled true with ServiceMonitor-default-true caveat. Differences list must include: HA service exposes only 26379, port name changes, UID 999 vs 1001 / no PVC reuse, emptyDir default if storage unset.
assertions: The translated values place the Sentinel configuration under the chart's HA mode block with 3 replicas, quorum 2, and downAfterMilliseconds 60000, and set the master group name to mymaster
The translated values raise the failover-wait/failover-timeout setting above the 60000 ms down-after value rather than leaving a default lower than it

Authentication is expressed as Valkey/Sentinel config-file fragments (e.g. requirepass/masterauth injected via extra config secrets for both the server and sentinel), not as a plain 'existingSecret: my-redis-secret' password field carried over unchanged
Persistence is expressed via the chart's storage size setting at 8Gi, and the answer states that leaving storage unset yields emptyDir (non-persistent) rather than a PVC
Metrics/exporter is enabled and the answer flags that the ServiceMonitor is created by default (unlike the Bitnami chart), so it may be created unintentionally
The behavioral-difference list states that the HA/Sentinel service exposes only the sentinel port 26379 (no direct 6379 endpoint) and that service/port naming differs from the Bitnami release
The behavioral-difference list states the container runs as UID 999 instead of Bitnami's 1001, and that existing Bitnami PVCs must not be reused/mounted as-is

evals.name: manage-everything-argo-cd-multi
evals.prompt: we manage everything with argo cd (multi-source apps, values files in a git repo). one app is a bitnami redis sentinel install (chart 21.x from charts.bitnami.com) that backs our container registry (sessions + job queues, several redis DB indexes). cluster is air-gapped. give me a migration plan to valkey: which chart, what to mirror, how to rewire the argo application, and how to move the data. write the plan to answer.md
evals.expected_output: Plan should: pick a Sentinel-capable chart (groundhog2k or CloudPirates, with reasoning; note official valkey-io chart lacks Sentinel), give the short mirror list (valkey/valkey image, oliver006/redis_exporter incl ghcr/quay, chart vendored, optionally redisshake binary/image), rewire Argo keeping the multi-source $values pattern (OCI repoURL without oci:// prefix, or vendored chart in git as bootstrap-safe), flag the circular dependency (registry's own dependency cannot be hosted by that registry), transfer data logically per DB index (RedisShake, verify per-DB), sequence sessions vs queue classes, and keep the final RDB as rollback.
assertions: Selects a Sentinel-capable Valkey chart (groundhog2k or CloudPirates) with stated reasoning, and states that the official valkey-io chart does not yet provide Sentinel-based automatic failover
Gives a concrete mirror list for the air-gapped registry that includes the valkey/valkey server image and a Redis/Valkey metrics exporter image, plus the chart artifact itself

Vendors the Valkey chart into git (or otherwise stores it outside the cluster's own registry) and explains that the registry cannot serve the chart for its own backing datastore's replacement — a circular bootstrap dependency

Keeps the existing Argo CD multi-source pattern with the values file repo referenced via $values, changing only the chart source away from charts.bitnami.com, and if an OCI registry is used states the repoURL omits the oci:// prefix
Deploys Valkey side-by-side under a new release name and repoints, rather than upgrading/replacing the Bitnami release in place
Moves the data with a logical replay tool (RedisShake or rdb-cli) covering all Redis DB indexes with per-DB verification, instead of REPLICAOF, RDB file copy, or DUMP/RESTORE from the running Redis
Distinguishes the session data from the job-queue data in the cutover sequence, treating queues as data that must be transferred or drained rather than discarded
Archives the final pre-cutover Redis RDB as the rollback artifact before deleting the Bitnami release and its PVCs
